title: feat(coding): the PR body is a fixed-size map for the reader, with decisions, proofs and agent notes collapsed under it
tldr: Coding-agent PR bodies grew with the diff: a median of 6,800 characters with seven embedded code blocks, and an 80-file PR at 26,600. The body is now a capped map (TL;DR, why, at most seven linked pointers, feedback wanted, risk, verified) with decisions, proofs and agent notes collapsed under it.
why: Reviewers spend their time understanding a change, and long descriptions predict fewer participants; a body that restates the diff spends that attention before the reader chooses where to look. Record [0050](https://github.com/acme/api/blob/main/docs/decisions/0050-the-pr-body-is-a-fixed-size-map-for-the-reader-and-everything-for-agents-sits-below-a-fold.md) argues the shape; this PR is its one unit.

pointers.label: The caps and the schema
pointers.text: Every map field is capped in visible characters and the pointers at seven; the tool refuses over the cap naming the field and the count.
pointers.risk: A cap counts `[label]` only, so a link's URL is free; check the regex does not swallow prose.

pointers.label: The renderer
pointers.text: The tldr with no heading, the bold labels, one numbered link row per pointer, then each fold as a `<details>` block, then the footer.
pointers.risk: Never a bare permalink line: that is what GitHub embeds as code.

pointers.label: The inverse parser
pointers.text: Reads the map by its labels and link rows, and a body in the previous contract by the old grammar, with `legacy Tour shape` as a problem.

pointers.label: The skill
pointers.text: `pr-description` replaces `pr-tour`: the map's fields and caps, how to choose seven pointers, the mechanical anchor rules, the fold.

pointers.label: The artifact keeps reading old records
pointers.text: `pr_description` carries `pointers` and `why`; a stored record that still says `tour` is accepted by the line parser.

pointers.label: The tests
pointers.text: Caps and counts named in the error, no bare permalink, a maximal map under 3,800 visible characters, the golden round trip, a legacy body.

feedbackWanted: Whether seven pointers and the per-field caps are the right numbers, and whether the review agent needs anything the Tour carried that the map does not.
risk: Every PR the coding agent opens from the next bot deploy renders the new shape; existing bodies are not rewritten and still parse. The change touches the type, both tool schemas, the prompt, the artifact and the run page's adapter; a miss shows up as a review run publishing `complete: false`.
verified: `npm run verify` green at head; the golden is this PR's own body rendered through the pipeline.

decisions.title: A refusal, not a truncation
decisions.rationale: A renderer that cut the surplus would publish a map the author never saw, which is the misaligned description the acceptance studies punish; a refusal costs one tool round-trip.

decisions.title: Inline links, never embeds
decisions.rationale: Seven embedded permalinks at the median PR is about 150 lines of code in the body, duplicating the Files tab where the reviewer can comment; a link lands on the same highlighted lines one click away.

decisions.title: The collapsed half is capped too
decisions.rationale: Otherwise the coverage instinct moves 14,000 characters into `<details>` and every reader of the whole body (the review agent, the artifact, `gh pr view`) pays anyway; the worst-case body is under 26,000 characters.

decisions.title: Remaining changes dropped
decisions.rationale: A file catalog restates the Files tab; the studies say the description should say why, and the diff already says what.

Both coding prompts name the map's fields and require loading `pr-description`; `pr-tour` appears nowhere

agentNotes: The golden fixture under `src/core/testing/` is this PR's own description rendered at the fixture repo `acme/api`; the Tour-shaped tests that pinned the previous contract were rewritten, not deleted, so every old assertion has a successor.
